about: Test cases for the new-password rules, run against both copies of them: passwordRules.test.ts runs them against auth/passwordRules.ts, and .github/scripts/rule-cases.mjs runs them against the API (PasswordRules.cs).

Without checkEmail, a case checks the length alone, like a reset link's form; the API run posts it to reset-password with a made-up token, where the length is checked before the token. With checkEmail, the case is for the account below, like the change password form; the API run changes that account's password (and puts it back after a case that's accepted).
error is the exact message, or null when the password is accepted. An empty password isn't here: the API refuses it before the password rules run ([Required]), with its own message.
A password is a string, or a list of parts joined together, where a part can be {"repeat": text, "count": n}.

cases.error: The password must be at least 12 characters.
The password can be at most 128 characters.

cases.case: spaces count toward the length: passwords aren't trimmed
six emoji are twelve characters, as .NET counts them (UTF-16)

cases.error: The password can't be your email address.
The password can't be your email address.

cases.case: the email with spaces around it
cases.error: The password can't be your email address.

cases.case: the email with U+0085 around it, which .NET trims
cases.error: The password can't be your email address.

cases.case: too short comes first, even when it's not the email
cases.error: The password must be at least 12 characters.

cases.case: the email and one more character is fine
